summary: The psalms describe people so beaten down that they need protection from a stronger party. The concrete sense of crushing survives in the term for a bodily injury.

senses.definition: Psalm 9 calls Yahweh a refuge for the oppressed. Psalm 10 places the oppressed beside the orphan who needs justice and relief from intimidation. A person reduced to such weakness may also suffer public shame.
Deuteronomy specifies an injury to the male reproductive organs by crushing, alongside severance, in its description of exclusion from the assembly. The word also occurs in the spelling דכא.

note: The noun for physical injury overlaps the forms indexed under דכא. Isaiah 57:15 describes a crushed person and Psalm 90:3 speaks of the human return to what is crushed or dust. Neither context describes the particular bodily injury in Deuteronomy.
